concepts.explanation: Compulsively reading bad news online even though it makes you feel worse.
AI-generated fake video or audio that makes someone appear to say or do things they never did.
Publishing someone's private information online, such as their address, to intimidate them.
Using a fake online identity to deceive someone, usually romantically.
Hidden parts of the internet reachable only with special software, used for anonymity and illegal markets.
A crypto scam where developers hype a token, then vanish with investors' money.
A blockchain token proving ownership of a digital item. Prices boomed and crashed in the early 2020s.
Content spreading extremely fast across the internet through shares.
Mass online withdrawal of support from a public figure after they say or do something offensive.
Someone who earns money by promoting products to their large social media following.
Organised operations running fake accounts to spread propaganda or manipulate opinion online.
Fake messages tricking people into revealing passwords or clicking malicious links.
A service that hides your location and encrypts your internet traffic.
Cutting off all contact with someone suddenly and without explanation.
Claiming to have woken up to a hidden truth. From The Matrix, now used across online subcultures.
Non-player character. Online insult for someone seen as having no independent thought.
A con artist, especially one running a long-term scam for money or attention.
A platform quietly hiding someone's posts from others without telling them.
A stock driven up by online hype rather than fundamentals, like GameStop in 2021.
